title: DeviceChain — Sparkplug Ingest
description: The Sparkplug B transport: whether the one reader is connected, what it receives, what it could not store, how presence is kept honest, and how commands to edge nodes fare. This service is optional. Start with the tiles: failures should stay at zero. Each instance gets its own copy of this board, scoped to it.

panels.title: Firing alerts
panels.description: Alerts firing right now for this instance. An empty table means none are firing. Alerts come from the instance's Prometheus rules, so the table stays empty if those rules are not installed.

panels.title: Active readers
panels.description: Replicas holding the Sparkplug leadership lease and connecting the sources. Exactly one is healthy: zero means no Sparkplug data is read at all, and more than one means duplicates. A pod deployed with no sources reads zero for good; configure its sources or leave the service out. This service is optional; when it is not installed the panel shows no data or zero.

panels.title: Broker connection failures, over the range
panels.description: Failed attempts to connect to a configured Sparkplug broker. The pod stays ready while a source is down, so this tile is how a bad host, a rejected credential or a broker outage shows. Above zero: the pod log names the source and the reason. This service is optional; when it is not installed the panel shows no data or zero.

panels.title: Subscriptions refused, over the range
panels.description: Sources abandoned and retried because the broker accepted the connection but refused, or never acknowledged, a group subscription. While any group is refused the source ingests none of its groups. Above zero: compare the credential's read permissions on the broker with the configured groups. This service is optional; when it is not installed the panel shows no data or zero.

panels.title: Messages dropped, over the range
panels.description: Accepted messages whose readings or presence changes were dropped after the retry budget, under backpressure or at shutdown. A Sparkplug host gets no redelivery, so each one is lost. Above zero: check device management, the message broker and the service log. This service is optional; when it is not installed the panel shows no data or zero.

panels.title: Undecodable messages, over the range
panels.description: Messages whose topic or payload could not be decoded. Above zero: a node or a bridge is publishing something that is not Sparkplug B. This service is optional; when it is not installed the panel shows no data or zero.

panels.title: Nodes that cannot register
panels.description: Nodes whose births could not be registered, most often because the source names a device type that does not exist yet. They are asked to rebirth. A standing non-zero value is a node, or a whole source, that is not registering; create the device type or fix the source. This service is optional; when it is not installed the panel shows no data or zero.

panels.title: Messages by type
panels.description: Sparkplug messages received per second by type (birth, data, death and so on). A flat line on a live fleet is the symptom of a lost subscription or a dead source. This service is optional; when it is not installed the panel shows no data or zero.

panels.title: Readings and presence stored
panels.description: Numeric readings written to the inbound-events stream per second, presence changes written per second, and devices auto-registered per second. Compare readings with the message rate above: messages arriving with no readings stored means they are being skipped or dropped. This service is optional; when it is not installed the panel shows no data or zero.

panels.title: Readings skipped, by reason
panels.description: Metrics of accepted messages that produced no reading, per second. non_numeric is a boolean, string or similar value and is normal; null, unnamed, untyped and oversize point at the node's configuration. An oversize message has none of its readings stored. This service is optional; when it is not installed the panel shows no data or zero.

panels.title: Messages and readings dropped
panels.description: Per second: messages dropped at ingest, undecodable messages, traffic from identities with no device while auto-registration is off, traffic for a tenant being deleted, readings older than 366 days, and readings shed because a tenant is over its ingest ceiling. A standing rate on any line is lost data. This service is optional; when it is not installed the panel shows no data or zero.

panels.title: Rebirth requests
panels.description: Rebirth commands per second: requested by the session machine, actually published, and discarded because the publish queue was full. Drops while published requests plateau means fan-out is outrunning a healthy publisher; drops while published is flat points at the broker connection. The liveness probe's rebirths count here too. This service is optional; when it is not installed the panel shows no data or zero.

panels.title: Liveness probes
panels.description: Probes that reached a verdict per second, by trigger. On a connected host the periodic series must rise; flat means the probe is not running, which a quiet fleet cannot tell apart. Connect probes run once per broker session. This service is optional; when it is not installed the panel shows no data or zero.

panels.title: Devices marked offline by a probe
panels.description: Devices a probe marked offline for not answering a rebirth, per second, by trigger. Near zero in a healthy fleet. A standing periodic rate means death certificates are being lost between the nodes and the host. This service is optional; when it is not installed the panel shows no data or zero.

panels.title: Registration recovery
panels.description: Nodes that could not be registered (left axis) and rebirths sent to them per second (right axis). A climbing rebirth rate beside a non-zero count is a registration that keeps failing. This service is optional; when it is not installed the panel shows no data or zero.

panels.title: Presence probe passes
panels.description: Passes of the periodic liveness probe per second by outcome, and the seconds since the last pass that completed, fully or partly. Failed or partial passes mean some nodes were not checked. This service is optional; when it is not installed the panel shows no data or zero.

panels.title: Presence probe pass time
panels.description: How long one pass of the periodic liveness probe takes (50th and 99th percentile). A pass that approaches the probe interval cannot keep up with the fleet. This service is optional; when it is not installed the panel shows no data or zero.

panels.title: Commands awaiting an outcome
panels.description: Published commands waiting for the node to report the requested value. Sparkplug has no acknowledgement, so a command is confirmed when the node reports the new value. Many waiting for a long time: nodes are slow to report, or the command path does not work. This service is optional; when it is not installed the panel shows no data or zero.

panels.title: Commands unconfirmed, over the range
panels.description: Commands that ended without the node reporting the requested value. They are recorded as timed out, not failed. A high share of published commands means the path does not work: check publish permission on the command topics and the host role. This service is optional; when it is not installed the panel shows no data or zero.

panels.title: Command faults, over the range
panels.description: Commands that could not be carried through: command-delivery unreachable or refusing the call, the awaiting store not writable, or a publish that may not have reached the node. Above zero: check command delivery, the message broker and the service log. This service is optional; when it is not installed the panel shows no data or zero.

panels.title: Command breaker trips, over the range
panels.description: Times a source's command breaker opened because the broker dropped the host session right after a command was published. Almost always a missing publish permission on the node and device command topics. While open, commands to that source fail at once. This service is optional; when it is not installed the panel shows no data or zero.

panels.title: Breakers not closed
panels.description: Sources whose command breaker is open or half-open right now. The source's telemetry is not affected; its commands fail fast until the breaker closes. This service is optional; when it is not installed the panel shows no data or zero.

panels.title: Commands by result
panels.description: Commands handled per second by result: published, confirmed, unconfirmed, parked, drained, refused_* before the wire, and the faults. Zero until a source enables commands. This service is optional; when it is not installed the panel shows no data or zero.

panels.title: Time to confirm a command
panels.description: Seconds from publishing a command to the node's report that confirms it (50th, 95th and 99th percentile). Commands that were never confirmed are not counted here. If the 99th percentile is near the confirmation window, raise the window or expect unconfirmed commands. This service is optional; when it is not installed the panel shows no data or zero.

panels.title: Command breaker state per source
panels.description: Each source's command breaker: 0 closed, 1 open (commands fail fast), 2 half-open (one command is let through). It closes only when the next command is published without a disconnect, so a source with no commands waiting stays half-open without alerting. This service is optional; when it is not installed the panel shows no data or zero.

list.name: namespace
list.label: Instance
list.description: The instance this board reads. Empty on purpose: the chart's templates/grafana-dashboard.yaml replaces this entry with a hidden constant naming the instance it installs, so every namespace="$namespace" selector reads that instance's series and no other. There is no instance picker: each instance ships its own copy of this board, in its own Grafana folder.

list.name: instance
list.label: Instance ID
list.description: The instance ID, used to select this instance's alerts. Empty on purpose: the chart's templates/grafana-dashboard.yaml replaces this entry with a hidden constant holding the ID of the instance it installs.
